瑠.meaning: A thief grabs the <part>king</part>'s blue jewel, but the stone seems to <part>detain</part> him all by itself: it's so heavy he can't lift it off its velvet cushion. The guards find him at dawn, still hugging it, gazing into the deep blue of the <kanji>lapis lazuli</kanji>.
瑠.on: A <sound>roo</sound>k on the window ledge caws at him all night.

璃.meaning: The <part>king</part> orders an <part>animal trap</part> made entirely of glass, so he can watch the beetles inside. It's so clear and smooth that the beetles can't climb out, and the king can't see it either, so he walks into it nose first. Everything about it is <kanji>glassy</kanji>.
璃.on: In a sulk, he sends it to the bottom of a coral <sound>ree</sound>f, where the fish admire their faces in it.

奈.meaning: In an old temple city sits a bronze statue so <part>large</part> that pigeons nest in its ears. Pilgrims climb the steps to the <part>altar</part> at its feet with flowers and rice cakes, and tame deer wander in to nibble them. You've arrived in <kanji>Nara</kanji>.
奈.on: A pilgrim leaves a warm <sound>na</sound>an on the altar, and a deer eats that too.
奈.kun: An <sound>ee</sound>l pops up in the temple pond with a pink <sound>carn</sound>ation in its mouth, and the pilgrims wonder what on earth it wants.

沙.meaning: A beach is so proud of its sand that it rinses every grain in <part>water drops</part> and keeps only a <part>few</part>: the tiniest, softest ones. The rest are sent off to a gravel pit. Step on what's left and it squeaks like flour: <kanji>fine sand</kanji>.
沙.on: A seagull digs a whole <sound>sa</sound>rdine out of it, still shiny.
沙.kun: Another gull shakes <sound>soo</sound>t off its wings and buries its <sound>na</sound>an in it for later.

汰.meaning: A <part>plump</part> raccoon sits by the stream and swirls every snack it finds through the <part>water drops</part>: grapes, crackers, a sock. Anything that falls apart wasn't food anyway. Supper always comes after a good <kanji>washing</kanji>.
汰.on: At home, it does the dishes in a big <sound>tu</sound>b.
汰.kun: It rinses a toy <sound>o</sound>ctopus and its swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles too, then pays for its friends' supper: a treat.

埼.meaning: A giant gardener digs a pond and tips the <part>soil</part> into the sea, but it piles up in a <part>strange</part> long finger of land pointing out over the waves. Ships steer round it and seals sunbathe on its tip: a brand-new <kanji>cape</kanji>.
埼.on: A seal finds a big brass <sound>key</sound> buried at the very tip.
埼.kun: The seals snack on <sound>sa</sound>rdines and a <sound>ki</sound>wi washed up from a shipwreck.

刹.meaning: An old gardener spends forty years trimming one <part>tree</part> with tiny <part>scissors</part>, and a <part>dagger</part> for the tricky bits. Branch by branch it becomes roofs, steps and bells, until monks move in and start chanting. The garden now has a living <kanji>temple</kanji>.
刹.on: A red <sound>set</sound>ter dog sleeps by its leafy gate.

茨.meaning: A donkey munches its way across a meadow of <part>grass</part>, always eyeing the <part>next</part> juicy patch, until its nose meets a tangle of hooked thorns. It backs off, braying. Every field has one corner nobody eats: the <kanji>briar</kanji>.
茨.on: The farmer cuts it back, hiding behind a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.
茨.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' squeals the donkey, and trots off to the farmer's <sound>ba</sound>rbecue to sulk over a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men.

梨.meaning: A farmer's only <part>tree</part> keeps dropping fat golden fruit onto passing cars. Instead of saying sorry, he sells the dented fruit as 'car-polished' and makes a huge <part>profit</part>. His fortune is all thanks to his <kanji>pear tree</kanji>.
梨.on: He spends it on a diving trip to a coral <sound>ree</sound>f.
梨.kun: Back home, he serves sliced pears on <sound>na</sound>an to his <sound>shee</sound>p.
